name: Weather station
tagline: Solar-ready micro environmental and precipitation station
summary: Eave mounts under roof eaves or balconies to measure ambient temperature, relative humidity, and non-contact precipitation or water reservoir levels via an ultrasonic transceiver. Designed for solar and battery powered long-range telemetry.

parts.name: ESP32 DevKit V1
parts.why: Dual-core processor with deep sleep power management and built-in WiFi/BLE.

parts.name: HC-SR04 Ultrasonic Distance Sensor
parts.why: 2cm - 400cm non-contact distance measurement for rainfall collection and cistern monitoring.

parts.name: DHT11 Temperature & Relative Humidity Sensor
parts.why: Digital calibrated environmental temperature and relative humidity probe.

parts.name: 0.96 inch I2C OLED Display
parts.why: Low-power field diagnostics HUD showing live sensor metrics.

parts.name: 18650 Li-ion Battery Holder with DC Jack
parts.why: Powers the station with rechargeable 3.7V/4.2V lithium-ion solar buffering.

product.pageHeadline: Microclimate weather telemetry right under your eaves.
bullets: Non-contact ultrasonic precipitation and water reservoir level measurement
Precision ambient temperature and humidity tracking via digital sensor
Designed for solar harvesting with low-power deep sleep cycles
Weather-resistant downward baffle slots prevent water ingress

buildSteps: Step 1: 3D print the Eave weather-baffled enclosure with outdoor-grade PETG or PLA.
Step 2: Install the twin transducers of the HC-SR04 into the front circular ports.
Step 3: Secure the ESP32 DevKit and DHT11 module inside the internal chassis.
Step 4: Wire trigger to GPIO5, echo to GPIO18, and DHT data to GPIO4.
Step 5: Connect 18650 battery holder to VIN/GND and route solar leads through the gland.
Step 6: Power on, mount beneath the eave, and calibrate ground/cistern baseline distance.
